papers.title: Deep learning-driven de novo design of ribosome binding sites in Paracoccus denitrificans.
papers.abstract: Paracoccus denitrificans is a heterotrophic nitrifying-aerobic denitrifying bacterium widely used in wastewater treatment and as a model system for studying electron transport chains, making it a promising chassis for environmental synthetic biology. Precise translational control of gene expression is essential for engineering desired traits in this organism, yet the design of functional ribosome binding sites (RBS) in P. denitrificans remains hindered by limited understanding of their sequence-activity relationships. To address this gap, we systematically profiled 1335 native RBS sequences vi
papers.summary: This study applies deep learning to design functional ribosome binding sites (RBS) in Paracoccus denitrificans, addressing a gap in translational control for this environmentally important bacterium. By profiling 1335 native RBS sequences, the authors develop a predictive model that enables de novo RBS design, potentially accelerating synthetic biology applications in wastewater treatment and related fields.

papers.title: FunVFPred: Predicting fungal virulence factors using a unified representation learning model.
papers.abstract: Fungal virulence factors (VFs) are proteins that support host colonization, tissue invasion, immune modulation, and disease progression. Identifying candidate VFs across pathogenic fungi can help characterize mechanisms underlying fungal-host interactions and prioritize proteins for experimental investigation. We developed FunVFPred, a machine learning framework that uses UniRep protein sequence embeddings, and multiple classifiers to predict candidate fungal VFs. Using experimentally validated VFs from human-pathogenic Candida species, the random forest model achieved 73.4% accuracy and a Mat
papers.summary: FunVFPred is a new machine learning tool that predicts fungal virulence factors using protein sequence embeddings, achieving 73.4% accuracy on Candida species. It offers a way to prioritize candidate virulence proteins for experimental study, potentially aiding research on fungal-host interactions and disease mechanisms.

papers.title: Frequency-filtered attention for cross-species fMRI time series prediction under small-sample learning.
papers.abstract: Functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) time series exhibit long-term temporal dependencies and stable functional connectivity (FC) structures. However, most existing prediction models mainly focus on the temporal domain, making it difficult to jointly capture spectral characteristics and neurobiological priors. We propose a general fMRI sequence prediction model, the Frequency-Filtered Attention Transformer (FFAformer). It models low-frequency variations in the frequency domain to capture long-range dependencies and incorporates FC consistency constraints to preserve brain network struct
papers.summary: The authors propose FFAformer, a Transformer-based model that captures long-range dependencies in fMRI time series by filtering low-frequency variations in the frequency domain and incorporating functional connectivity consistency constraints. This approach improves cross-species fMRI prediction under small-sample learning conditions, addressing limitations of existing temporal-only models.

papers.title: LncPNdeep: A long non-coding RNA classifier based on large language model with peptide and nucleotide embedding.
papers.abstract: Accurate classification of long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) is essential for transcriptome annotation and understanding gene regulation. Existing computational methods predominantly rely on nucleotide sequence features, frequently overlooking biologically relevant peptide signals encoded within lncRNAs. To overcome this limitation, we developed LncPNdeep, an integrative deep learning framework that combines nucleotide and peptide embeddings extracted via masked language models, specifically utilizing contextual representations from BigBird, Longformer, and ProtTrans. By fusing both features in a
papers.summary: LncPNdeep is a new deep learning classifier that improves lncRNA identification by combining both nucleotide sequence and peptide-level features extracted from large language models (BigBird, Longformer, ProtTrans). This integrative approach outperforms methods that rely only on nucleotide sequences, capturing biologically relevant peptide signals often overlooked in existing tools.

papers.title: LLM-powered Functional Gene Set Summarization with genesetGPT.
papers.abstract: Transcriptomics datasets generated using next-generation sequencing techniques such as single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatially-resolved transcriptomics (SRT) allow researchers to study patterns in gene expression across celltypes, temporal processes, and spatial organization at ever-higher resolutions and depths. scRNA-seq analyses produce gene expression profiles and celltype-specific gene sets that require annotation to provide biological meaning, a process that has traditionally relied on the manual interpretations of clinical scientists. Similarly, SRT experiments typically re
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: genesetGPT is a new LLM-powered tool that automatically generates plain-language summaries of gene sets from transcriptomics data, such as those from single-cell and spatial experiments, replacing slow manual annotation. It helps researchers quickly understand the biological meaning of their gene lists, making analysis more efficient and accessible.

papers.title: BioPathfinder: Evidence-guided multi-agent platform enables hypothesis discovery for CAR-T engineering.
papers.abstract: Clinical studies of chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T therapy generate diverse molecular and clinical evidence that remains fragmented across publications, public repositories and patient-derived datasets, limiting systematic therapeutic discovery. Here we present BioPathfinder, an evidence-guided multi-agent workflow for closed-loop biomedical discovery. BioPathfinder constructs a provenance-aware knowledge resource linking publications with patient single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) datasets and clinical metadata, and uses role-specialized large language model agents to generate, review
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: BioPathfinder is a new multi-agent platform that integrates fragmented CAR-T therapy evidence from publications, patient single-cell RNA-seq data, and clinical metadata into a provenance-aware knowledge resource. It uses specialized large language model agents to generate and review hypotheses, enabling systematic therapeutic discovery for CAR-T engineering.

papers.title: Sequence determinants of pathogenicity in glucose-6-phosphatase linked to glycogen storage disease type 1a.
papers.abstract: Glycogen storage disease type 1a (GSD1a) is an autosomal recessive Mendelian disorder that can be caused by missense variants in glucose-6-phosphatase catalytic subunit 1 (G6PC1). Although hundreds of missense variants have been identified, the vast majority are of unknown clinical significance, and the molecular mechanism(s) of bona fide pathogenic variants are ill-defined. We combine bioinformatic data and clinical associations with the protein language model AlphaMissense to guide mechanistic exploration of 78 missense variants at 55 residue positions using robust biochemical and biophysica
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint investigates the molecular mechanisms underlying pathogenicity of missense variants in G6PC1, the gene associated with glycogen storage disease type 1a. By combining bioinformatic predictions (including AlphaMissense) with biochemical and biophysical characterization of 78 variants, the authors aim to define sequence determinants that distinguish pathogenic from benign variants, potentially improving variant interpretation.

papers.title: Early Detection Methods for Autism Spectrum Disorder: From Clinical Screening to Multimodal AI.
papers.abstract: Early detection of autism spectrum disorder (ASD) in young children is essential for timely referral, developmental monitoring, and access to early intervention. However, conventional screening and diagnostic pathways often depend on parent-report instruments, episodic clinical observation, and specialist-administered assessments, which may delay identification during the first years of life. This scoping review maps the methodological landscape of early ASD detection from traditional clinical screening to multimodal artificial intelligence (AI). A structured literature search was conducted ac
papers.summary: This scoping review maps the landscape of early autism spectrum disorder (ASD) detection methods, from traditional clinical screening tools to emerging multimodal artificial intelligence approaches. It highlights the limitations of conventional parent-report and specialist-based assessments and discusses how AI could improve early identification, though the review is descriptive rather than presenting new empirical findings.

papers.title: Persistent Manifold Learning of Protein Properties.
papers.abstract: Predicting how tightly two biomolecules bind remains a major challenge, in part because different interaction classes present dissimilar interfaces, from compact metal-coordinated pockets to broad, featureless protein surfaces. We introduce persistent manifold learning (PML), a novel computational framework that describes a binding interface as a family of multiscale manifolds. Boundary-Induced Graph Laplacian, a discrete realization of de Rham-Hodge theory, then extracts topological invariants together with nonharmonic spectral information, capturing the geometry of an interface as well as it
papers.summary: This paper introduces persistent manifold learning (PML), a new computational framework that models protein binding interfaces as multiscale manifolds and uses a discrete de Rham-Hodge theory approach to extract topological and spectral features. The method aims to improve predictions of biomolecular binding affinity across diverse interaction types, from small metal-coordinated pockets to large protein surfaces.

papers.title: Left ventricular hypertrophy as a predictor of adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes in chronic hypertension in pregnancy: a multicenter study.
papers.abstract: The impact of chronic hypertension (CHTN) combined with left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) on adverse maternal and fetal pregnancy outcomes remains unclear.
papers.summary: This multicenter study investigates whether left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) in pregnant women with chronic hypertension predicts worse maternal and neonatal outcomes. The findings clarify the prognostic value of LVH in this high-risk population, potentially guiding closer monitoring and management.

papers.title: Enhanced classification and identification of bacterial and viral microorganisms by integration of MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry with artificial intelligence.
papers.abstract: The accurate and rapid identification of bacterial pathogens is essential in clinical setups and medical biodefense. Matrix-Assisted Laser Desorption Ionization Time-Of-Flight (MALDI-TOF) mass spectrometry has emerged as a powerful tool for fast and reliable microbial identification. This study assesses the performance of eight Machine Learning (ML) and two Deep Learning (DL) models trained using 5-fold cross validation in classifying microorganisms in a series of experiments based on MALDI-TOF mass spectra (n = 255) generated internally from seven cultured bacteria and five viral agents. The
papers.summary: This study evaluates machine learning and deep learning models for classifying bacteria and viruses from MALDI-TOF mass spectra, achieving accurate identification of seven bacterial and five viral agents. The integration of AI with MALDI-TOF enhances the speed and reliability of microbial pathogen identification, which is critical for clinical diagnostics and biodefense.

papers.title: Advances in multimodal data integration for drug efficacy prediction: Methodological evolution and clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Drug efficacy prediction remains a cornerstone of drug development and precision therapy. However, integrating heterogeneous biomedical data, including multi-omics profiles, pathological imaging, electronic health records, and pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) time-series, faces three fundamental barriers, namely cross-domain distribution shifts between preclinical and clinical data, relational mismatches between isolated vector representations and biological networks, and feature heterogeneity across disparate modalities. To address these challenges, three AI paradigms have emerged, tra
papers.summary: This review discusses recent advances in multimodal data integration for drug efficacy prediction, highlighting three key challenges—cross-domain distribution shifts, relational mismatches, and feature heterogeneity—and the AI paradigms developed to address them. It emphasizes the methodological evolution from early approaches to current deep learning frameworks and their potential for clinical translation in precision therapy.

papers.title: PhaseOM: an integrated multi-task framework for phase separation analysis and key residue detection.
papers.abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) drives cellular organization through scaffold proteins that initiate condensate formation and client proteins that partition into them. Current computational tools lack precision in differentiating these functional classes and identifying key intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs), limiting mechanistic understanding of LLPS in health and disease.
papers.summary: PhaseOM is a new computational framework that integrates multiple tasks to analyze liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS), improving the classification of scaffold versus client proteins and the identification of key intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) involved in condensate formation. This tool addresses limitations in existing methods and could enhance mechanistic understanding of LLPS in health and disease.

papers.title: Bile extracellular vesicles for early cholangiocarcinoma detection in primary sclerosing cholangitis.
papers.abstract: Cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) is a major complication of primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC), with a 20-year incidence of ∼15%. Early detection is challenging, as current surveillance rarely identifies CCA at a resectable stage. This study investigated bile-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) as a liquid biopsy source for protein biomarkers enabling early diagnosis and prediction of CCA in PSC.
papers.summary: This study explores bile-derived extracellular vesicles (EVs) as a liquid biopsy for early detection of cholangiocarcinoma (CCA) in patients with primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC). The authors identify protein biomarkers within bile EVs that could enable earlier diagnosis and prediction of CCA, potentially improving surveillance and outcomes in this high-risk population.

papers.title: Interpretable distillation reveals that deep learning splicing models suffer from pervasive confounders and blind spots.
papers.abstract: Predicting RNA splicing from genomic sequence is a crucial task for understanding gene regulation and interpreting genetic variation. Recent deep learning advancements have led to splicing prediction algorithms that achieve state-of-the-art performance compared to earlier models. However, owing to the limited interpretability of deep learning models, the predictive mechanisms of current splicing models remain poorly understood.
papers.summary: This paper investigates the interpretability of deep learning models for RNA splicing prediction, revealing that these models are affected by pervasive confounders and have blind spots in their predictive mechanisms. The authors use interpretable distillation to uncover these issues, highlighting limitations in current state-of-the-art splicing models.

papers.title: Geneformer-guided multiomics integration identifies Pbx1 as a network hub of hematopoietic stem cell aging.
papers.abstract: Hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs) constitute an organized hematopoietic system that undergoes age-related alterations, including increased platelet production and decreased erythropoiesis. The fundamental mechanisms driving these shifts remain incompletely understood. We used single-cell RNA sequencing data to show that old HSCs contain two distinct transcriptional programs: one shared with megakaryocytes and the other reflecting the most primitive HSC state. Developmental time-series profiling further suggests that the acquisition of these programs begins early in life, with the primitive modul
papers.summary: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing and the Geneformer deep learning model to identify two distinct transcriptional programs in aged hematopoietic stem cells (HSCs), one linked to megakaryocytes and one to the primitive HSC state. The authors pinpoint Pbx1 as a key network hub driving HSC aging, with developmental time-series data suggesting these aging programs begin early in life.

papers.title: Machine learning of sunitinib resistance genes reveals that SP5 regulates angiogenesis and sunitinib resistance in RCC via the VEGFA/AKT axis.
papers.abstract: Sunitinib resistance remains a major clinical challenge in renal cell carcinoma, and the underlying molecular mechanisms are incompletely understood. SP5, a member of the specificity protein transcription factor family, has been implicated in tumor progression, but its role in sunitinib resistance and angiogenesis in RCC is unclear.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning to identify genes associated with sunitinib resistance in renal cell carcinoma (RCC), revealing that the transcription factor SP5 promotes angiogenesis and resistance to sunitinib through the VEGFA/AKT signaling axis. The findings provide a potential new target for overcoming sunitinib resistance in RCC.

papers.title: PregBase: A comprehensive knowledge base for clinically relevant knowledge representation and biomarker prediction in pregnancy.
papers.abstract: Pregnancy complications are a leading cause of maternal and neonatal mortality worldwide. Understanding their underlying mechanisms is hindered by dispersed evidence across thousands of studies and complex biological interactions. We present PregBase, a comprehensive knowledge base for pregnancy research comprising automated extraction, validation, and exploration. PregBase was constructed by utilising large language models (LLMs) to extract relationships from literature; 13 LLMs were benchmarked across seven prompting strategies, with ensemble shuffle prompting outperforming single-strategy a
papers.summary: PregBase is a new knowledge base for pregnancy research that uses large language models to automatically extract and validate relationships from the scientific literature. The authors benchmarked 13 LLMs with seven prompting strategies, finding that ensemble shuffle prompting was most effective, and the resulting resource supports biomarker prediction and clinical knowledge representation for pregnancy complications.

papers.title: AI-Guided Computational Design of Synthetic Microbiota for Next-Generation Immunomodulatory Applications.
papers.abstract: The growing recognition of the human microbiome as a key regulator of immune homeostasis has accelerated the application of computational intelligence for microbiome-driven disease understanding and therapeutic design. However, existing microbiome studies largely rely on classical machine learning or shallow deep learning models that fail to capture higher-order microbial interactions, multimodal functional dependencies, and immune feasibility constraints simultaneously. Moreover, most approaches lack biological constraint enforcement, leading to predictions that may be statistically accurate
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of AI-guided computational design for synthetic microbiota aimed at immunomodulatory applications, highlighting the limitations of current machine learning and shallow deep learning models in capturing complex microbial interactions and immune constraints. It emphasizes the need for more advanced computational approaches that enforce biological constraints to improve therapeutic design.

papers.title: Bridging Linguistic Reasoning and Biophysical Reality Toward Peptide Engineering via Instruction-Tuned Language Modelling.
papers.abstract: Peptides serve as critical mediators in biological systems, regulating essential processes ranging from neurotransmission to immune response. However, their nonlinear sequence-function relationships and immense chemical diversity pose significant challenges for efficient experimental characterization and therapeutic development. While Protein Language Models have advanced biological sequence understanding, they predominantly capture global evolutionary features of full-length proteins, often overlooking the local physicochemical dependencies and short-range residue interactions that are essent
papers.summary: This paper presents an instruction-tuned language model approach for peptide engineering that bridges linguistic reasoning with biophysical reality. The model is designed to capture local physicochemical dependencies and short-range residue interactions that are essential for peptide function, addressing limitations of standard protein language models that focus on global evolutionary features of full-length proteins.

papers.title: Deep learning enabled prediction of nuclear lamina-associated chromatin.
papers.abstract: Tethering of chromatin regions to the nuclear lamina contributes to genome organization and gene regulation. Though several molecular and epigenomic determinants of lamina association have been studied, the influence of genomic sequences has received less attention. Here, we present lamina-associated domain finder (LADDER), a multimodal deep learning model to predict lamina association based on DNA sequence, gene density, and long interspersed nuclear element (LINE)1 and short interspersed nuclear element (SINE) densities. The predictions made by LADDER are cell-type independent. Using LADDER'
papers.summary: This paper introduces LADDER, a multimodal deep learning model that predicts nuclear lamina-associated chromatin domains using DNA sequence, gene density, and LINE1/SINE repeat densities. The model's predictions are cell-type independent, suggesting that sequence features alone can capture lamina association, providing a new tool for studying genome organization and gene regulation.

papers.title: BioMaster: Multi-agent system for automated bioinformatics analysis workflow.
papers.abstract: The growing volume and complexity of biological data have made bioinformatics workflows increasingly labor-intensive, error-prone, and difficult to scale. Large language model-based agents offer potential for automation but often fail in complex, multi-step analyses because of limited robustness. We present BioMaster, a multi-agent framework that integrates workflow planning, execution, error recovery, and output validation. BioMaster incorporates a dual retrieval-augmented design to leverage domain knowledge for tool selection, parameterization, and adaptation across tasks. A dedicated debug
papers.summary: BioMaster is a multi-agent framework that automates complex bioinformatics workflows by integrating planning, execution, error recovery, and validation. It uses a dual retrieval-augmented design to improve tool selection and parameterization, addressing robustness issues in large language model-based agents for multi-step analyses.

papers.title: Brain-AI convergence: Generative world models and hierarchical attention for human intelligence.
papers.abstract: Recent advances in general-purpose AI provide new insights into how the neocortex and cerebellum, despite their uniform circuit architectures, support diverse functions and human intelligence. Beyond the traditional focus on visual processing, this paper offers a cross-domain comparison of the brain and AI through the lens of world-model-based computation. We argue that both the neocortex and cerebellum predict future world states from past inputs and construct predictive world models through prediction-error learning. These predictive world models are repurposed for sensory comprehension and
papers.summary: This paper proposes a cross-domain framework comparing brain computation with modern AI, arguing that both the neocortex and cerebellum operate as generative world models that predict future states via prediction-error learning, and that hierarchical attention mechanisms in AI mirror brain processes underlying human intelligence. It extends the brain-AI analogy beyond vision to diverse cognitive functions, offering a unified perspective on how uniform neural circuits support flexible intelligence.

papers.title: Computationally Evidence-Grounded Sequence-First Design of Peptide Binders.
papers.abstract: Peptide binders provide a versatile modality for modulating protein targets that are poorly addressed by small molecules, but their discovery is constrained by sample-intensive screening or reliance on structural templates. Sequence-first generation offers a scalable alternative for targets lacking stable or representative structures, yet existing approaches often sacrifice target-specific control for diversity and are further limited by the imperfect transfer of protein language-model priors to short peptides. Here, we report BOND-PEP, an evidence-grounded framework for sequence-only peptide
papers.summary: The paper introduces BOND-PEP, a computational framework for designing peptide binders using only sequence information, without requiring structural templates. It addresses limitations of existing sequence-first methods by improving target-specific control and adapting protein language models to short peptides, offering a scalable alternative for targets lacking stable structures.

papers.title: HTS-Oracle X: AI-Guided Prospective Discovery of Small Molecule Immune Checkpoint Binders.
papers.abstract: Targeting immune checkpoint protein-protein interactions (PPIs) using small molecules remains limited by the characteristically low hit rates of conventional high-throughput screening against these interfaces. Here we report HTS-Oracle X, a multimodal deep learning platform that integrates bidirectional cross-attention fusion of ChemBERTa SMILES embeddings with extended RDKit descriptors, trains on continuous biophysical binding signals rather than binary labels, and employs Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty quantification for uncertainty-adjusted compound selection. Trained on 45,760 Dianthus T
papers.summary: HTS-Oracle X is a multimodal deep learning platform that integrates ChemBERTa SMILES embeddings with RDKit descriptors and uses continuous biophysical binding signals with Monte Carlo Dropout uncertainty to improve prospective discovery of small-molecule immune checkpoint binders. It addresses the low hit rates of conventional high-throughput screening against protein-protein interaction interfaces.

papers.title: Benchmarking Classical and Quantum Machine Learning for Potency Prediction across Ten Therapeutically Relevant Targets.
papers.abstract: Quantum machine learning (QML) is widely proposed as a successor to classical models in cheminformatics, but rigorous benchmarks under realistic contemporary data constraints remain scarce. We compared two quantum classifiers (quantum support vector machine, variational quantum classifier) against gradient boosting, random forest, and neural network baselines across ten therapeutically diverse protein targets (45-18,286 compounds), using Bemis-Murcko scaffold-stratified cross-validation. Across 48 valid target-threshold tasks, no model class globally dominated (best-quantum versus best-classic
papers.summary: This study benchmarks quantum machine learning classifiers against classical models for potency prediction across ten therapeutic targets, finding no global performance advantage for quantum methods under realistic data constraints. The results suggest that classical models remain competitive, highlighting the need for careful evaluation of QML in cheminformatics.

papers.title: Peptide language pragmatic analysis and two-stage hierarchical learning framework for therapeutic peptide prediction.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic peptides exert pivotal effects in diverse biological processes, and have attracted significant interest in the field of biomedicine in recent years. However, most existing methods often fail to adequately capture the intricate interactions among amino acid residues and the contextual dependencies within peptide sequences, which hampers the extraction of deep semantic representations and ultimately restricts predictive performance. Moreover, the task of multi-functional therapeutic peptide prediction is inherently constrained by the challenge of imbalanced multi-label classification
papers.summary: This paper introduces a new computational framework that uses a peptide language model and a two-stage hierarchical learning approach to improve the prediction of therapeutic peptides and their functions. The method better captures amino acid interactions and sequence context, addressing limitations of existing tools and handling the challenge of imbalanced multi-label classification.

papers.title: Transforming subcellular spatial transcriptomics: deep learning models for cell segmentation.
papers.abstract: Subcellular spatial transcriptomics (SSTs) is transforming biology by revealing where individual RNA molecules are located within intact tissues, providing unprecedented insight into how cells function and interact. Achieving this promise depends on accurately identifying the boundaries of individual cells, making cell segmentation one of the field's central computational challenges. A core methodological issue is how best to ensure correct and biologically accurate assignment of transcripts to cells using cell segmentation algorithms. Recent advances in deep learning models have been instrume
papers.summary: This review discusses the central challenge of cell segmentation in subcellular spatial transcriptomics (SSTs), emphasizing the need for accurate assignment of RNA molecules to individual cells. It highlights recent advances in deep learning models that are instrumental in improving segmentation accuracy and biological fidelity.

papers.title: DeepPNI: a language- and graph-based model for mutation-driven protein-nucleic acid binding energetics.
papers.abstract: Protein-nucleic acid interactions (PNIs) are central to fundamental biological processes, and mutations can disrupt these interactions by altering local structural features and binding free energy. Here, we present DeepPNI, a deep learning regression model that integrates sequence- and structure-based features to estimate mutation-induced changes in binding free energy in protein-nucleic acid complexes. The model was developed using a comprehensive dataset of 1754 mutations spanning protein-DNA and protein-RNA complexes, representing one of the largest curated datasets for PNI binding free ene
papers.summary: DeepPNI is a new deep learning model that predicts how mutations affect the binding strength of protein-nucleic acid interactions by combining sequence and structural features. It was trained on a large curated dataset of 1,754 mutations in protein-DNA and protein-RNA complexes, making it a valuable tool for understanding mutation effects in these critical biological processes.

papers.title: DNAreader: accurate prediction of DNA-binding residues in structured and disordered proteins using transformers and contrastive learning.
papers.abstract: Accurate predictions of DNA-binding residues (DBRs) in protein sequences facilitate decoding molecular-level mechanisms underlying cellular functions that involve protein-DNA interactions. While dozens of these predictors have been released, they target either structured or intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs), and the latter were trained to predict less detailed DNA-binding IDRs rather than DBRs. Given this dichotomy, the structure-trained methods underperform on disordered proteins, and vice versa. Moreover, they suffer from high cross-prediction rates, incorrectly labeling many residues
papers.summary: DNAreader is a new deep learning tool that accurately predicts DNA-binding residues in both structured and disordered proteins, overcoming the limitations of existing predictors that specialize in only one type. It uses transformers and contrastive learning to reduce false positive predictions and provides a unified solution for identifying DNA-binding residues across the entire protein sequence.

papers.title: AI semantics for biomedical data integration.
papers.abstract: Researchers increasingly need to explore hypotheses that span multimodal data across different scales, organisms, and domains. In practice, this requires connecting knowledge across fragmented databases with incompatible APIs and heterogeneous annotation practices. Large language model (LLM) agents can automate this data integration process, but grounding LLM agent outputs in scientifically correct sources of truth remains a significant challenge. Here we describe our deployment of a novel AI semantics workflow using LLM agents to enable scalable data integration, grounded in biological knowle
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint describes a novel AI semantics workflow that uses large language model (LLM) agents to automate the integration of multimodal biomedical data from fragmented databases with incompatible APIs and heterogeneous annotations. The workflow grounds LLM agent outputs in biological knowledge to ensure scientific correctness, addressing a key challenge in scalable data integration.

papers.title: Tau reduction counteracts transcriptomic and behavioral abnormalities in an Alzheimer amyloid model.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) causes amyloid formation, neuritic dystrophy, gliosis, synapse loss, behavioral abnormalities, and weight loss. 5xFAD transgenic mice simulate these alterations. To further investigate overall tau reduction as a therapeutic strategy for AD-related abnormalities, we compared 5xFAD mice carrying 2, 1, or 0 Mapt alleles encoding endogenous wildtype tau. Behavioral alterations in 5xFAD mice detected by a machine learning algorithm were prevented or minimized by tau reduction, although 5xFAD/ Mapt +/+ mice had no classical tau pathology. Reduction of nonfibrillar tau also p
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: This preprint shows that reducing endogenous tau levels in 5xFAD Alzheimer's model mice prevents or minimizes behavioral abnormalities and transcriptomic changes, even though these mice lack classical tau pathology. The findings suggest that nonfibrillar tau plays a key role in mediating amyloid-driven dysfunction, supporting tau reduction as a potential therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: HaloMPNN: retraining ProteinMPNN on halophilic proteomes for salt-tolerant enzyme design.
papers.abstract: Machine learning-guided protein sequence redesign is now routinely used to optimize multiple properties relevant for protein engineering, most prominently thermostability and recombinant expression levels. Salt tolerance is a valuable property for "blue-biotechnology"- enabled biomanufacturing, yet no generative computational method exists to redesign proteins for increased salt tolerance. We hypothesized that a training dataset heavily biased toward salt-adapted proteomes would yield a model capable of designing proteins with halophilic properties. To test this, we retrained the sequence rede
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: The authors introduce HaloMPNN, a retrained version of ProteinMPNN using halophilic proteomes, to enable computational design of salt-tolerant enzymes. This is the first generative method for redesigning proteins with increased salt tolerance, addressing a gap in protein engineering for blue biotechnology.

papers.title: Recombinant SpTrf proteins illustrate putative functions of native SpTrf proteins: from immune response to resolution in sea urchins.
papers.abstract: The complex and sophisticated sea urchin innate immune system relies on conserved immune receptor and effector molecules plus the euechinoid-specific Transformer family. Native SpTransformer (natSpTrf) proteins in Strongylocentrotus purpuratus respond to immune challenge by augmenting phagocytosis of microbes. These proteins show significant sequence diversity both within and among sea urchins with the predicted benefit of host protection through the recognition of a broad range of pathogens. Prior reports show that 6 recombinant (r)SpTrf proteins from insect cells induce phagocytosis when cro
papers.summary: This study investigates the functions of recombinant SpTransformer (rSpTrf) proteins from sea urchins, showing that they can enhance phagocytosis and may play roles in immune response and resolution. The findings suggest that the diverse SpTrf family contributes to broad pathogen recognition and immune regulation in sea urchins.

papers.title: Fine-grained structural classification of biosynthetic gene cluster-encoded products.
papers.abstract: Biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs) are responsible the biosynthesis of many natural products, including a multitude of effective therapeutics and their precursors. Advances in genomic data collection as well as computational techniques have made it possible to identify BGCs at scale. However, accurately determining the types of BGC-encoded products from genomic content remains elusive.
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational method for fine-grained structural classification of products encoded by biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), addressing the challenge of accurately determining natural product types from genomic data. The approach improves upon existing tools by enabling more detailed categorization of BGC-encoded compounds, which is crucial for discovering novel therapeutics.

papers.title: Identification and Experimental Validation of Key Genes Related to Neuroendocrine in Periodontitis Based on Single-Cell and Bulk Transcriptome Data.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory condition linked to systemic diseases, yet the neuroendocrine mechanisms underlying its pathogenesis remain unclear. This study aimed to elucidate neuroendocrine-related molecular pathways involved in periodontitis. Transcriptomic data and neuroendocrine-related genes (NRGs) were integrated to identify candidate genes from the overlap between differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and NRGs. Machine learning, ROC analysis and expression validation were used to screen key genes and construct a diagnostic nomogram. Functional enrichment, immune infiltration,
papers.journal: Journal of cellular and molecular medicine
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data to identify neuroendocrine-related genes involved in periodontitis, using machine learning and ROC analysis to pinpoint key diagnostic genes. The authors validated these genes experimentally and constructed a nomogram, revealing potential neuroendocrine-immune interactions in the disease.

papers.title: Structure-aware deep learning enhances m6A prediction and reveals cell type-associated RNA structural signatures.
papers.abstract: N6-methyladenosine (m6A), the most abundant mRNA modification in eukaryotes, plays essential roles in gene regulation and disease pathogenesis. Computational prediction of m6A sites offers a scalable alternative to costly experimental approaches, yet current methods rely predominantly on linear sequence features. This overlooks potentially informative RNA structural context, which is associated with local methylation patterns and may provide complementary predictive information beyond linear sequence motifs. To incorporate this complementary information, we propose SMART-m6A (Sequence-structur
papers.summary: The authors introduce SMART-m6A, a deep learning method that integrates RNA structural information with sequence data to improve prediction of m6A modification sites. The approach reveals cell type-associated RNA structural signatures, demonstrating that structural context provides complementary predictive power beyond linear sequence motifs.

papers.title: scKanFormer: A Transformer-KAN framework with biologically informed attention for cell type annotation in large-scale scRNA-seq data.
papers.abstract: A key challenge in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data analysis is accurately and efficiently identifying the cell type of each cell. Cell type annotation for scRNA-seq data not only needs to overcome batch effects caused by various factors but also requires effective handling of large-scale scRNA-seq datasets. Although deep learning has achieved remarkable progress in cell type annotation tasks, it still exhibits limitations in interpretability and robustness against batch effects. To tackle these issues, we propose a supervised framework based on the Transformer architecture, named s
papers.summary: This paper introduces scKanFormer, a Transformer-based framework enhanced with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) and biologically informed attention for cell type annotation in large-scale scRNA-seq data. The method improves interpretability and robustness against batch effects compared to existing deep learning approaches, addressing key limitations in current annotation tools.

papers.title: An integrated systems biology and machine learning framework for identifying potential biomarkers and pathways in autism spectrum disorder.
papers.abstract: Autism spectrum disorders (ASD) are a group of neurodevelopmental disorders whose underlying molecular mechanisms and biological processes remain incompletely understood. In this study, we used a multi-layered systems biology approach to prioritize candidate genes and regulatory factors associated with ASD.
papers.summary: This study applies a multi-layered systems biology approach combined with machine learning to identify potential biomarkers and key pathways in autism spectrum disorder (ASD). By integrating genomic and transcriptomic data, the authors prioritize candidate genes and regulatory factors that may contribute to ASD pathogenesis, offering new insights into the disorder's molecular basis.

papers.title: The impact of SGLT2 inhibitors on uric acid levels in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction: integration of mechanisms and clinical evidence.
papers.abstract: Hyperuricemia (HUA) is a prevalent comorbidity in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and is closely associated with disease progression and adverse outcomes. Sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors can rapidly and sustainably reduce serum uric acid (SUA) levels and lower the incidence of HUA-related clinical events; however, their underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study employed network pharmacology and molecular docking to systematically investigate the potential mechanisms of SGLT2 inhibitors in HFpEF patients with concomitant hyperuricemi
papers.summary: This review/study examines how SGLT2 inhibitors lower uric acid levels in heart failure patients with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) and hyperuricemia, using network pharmacology and molecular docking to explore potential mechanisms. It highlights that SGLT2 inhibitors rapidly and sustainably reduce serum uric acid and related clinical events, though the underlying pathways are not fully understood.

papers.title: SPOCK1 overexpression suggests poor prognosis in head and neck squamous cell carcinomas.
papers.abstract: Head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCCs) are mostly associated with smoking, alcohol intake, and/or human papillomavirus HPV16 and/or HPV18 infection. However, most tumors are diagnosed at an advanced stage. In the search for biomarkers of HNSCC, we studied the prognostic role of SPOCK1, a heparan sulfate proteoglycan. In HNSCC, SPOCK1 expression was tested both at in silico mRNA level using the Kaplan-Meier Plotter and at in situ protein level after SPOCK1 immunohistochemistry after whole slide digitalization. Protein expression results were analyzed using H-Scores, both by eye-control
papers.summary: This study investigates SPOCK1, a heparan sulfate proteoglycan, as a potential prognostic biomarker in head and neck squamous cell carcinomas (HNSCC). Using in silico mRNA analysis and immunohistochemistry, the authors found that high SPOCK1 expression is associated with poor prognosis in HNSCC patients, suggesting its potential utility as a prognostic marker.

papers.title: Recent advances in deep learning for leukemia diagnosis: a scoping review of diagnostic modalities and fusion-based approaches.
papers.abstract: The diagnosis of leukemia is inherently a multimodal process that combines morphological evaluation, immunophenotyping, molecular profiling and standard laboratory tests. Deep learning techniques have been adopted across all components of the diagnostic process over the past few years, particularly in microscopic image analysis. However, current research and review articles are highly fragmented, and most methods are limited to the single data modalities and benchmark-based performance analysis, which provide a limited understanding of model generalizations, clinical and real-world applicabili
papers.summary: This scoping review surveys deep learning applications across the multimodal diagnostic workflow for leukemia, including image analysis, immunophenotyping, and molecular profiling. It highlights the fragmentation of current research, which is largely limited to single-modality, benchmark-based studies, and emphasizes the need for fusion-based approaches and better clinical generalization.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and experimental validation links effector chondrocyte-associated oxidative stress to EIF6-related p47phox-NOX2 signaling in osteoarthritis.
papers.abstract: Oxidative stress is closely involved in osteoarthritis (OA), but the cell-type-specific oxidative stress landscape and related regulatory molecules in human cartilage remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to identify effector chondrocyte (EC)-associated oxidative stress features in OA and to prioritize candidate molecules linked to p47phox-NOX2-related ROS responses.
papers.summary: This study uses integrated single-cell analysis and experimental validation to characterize the oxidative stress landscape in human osteoarthritis cartilage, identifying effector chondrocytes as a key cell type. The authors link EIF6 to p47phox-NOX2-mediated reactive oxygen species signaling, proposing a novel regulatory mechanism in OA pathogenesis.

papers.title: Decoding serum C-reactive protein-associated molecular patterns in aging and secondhand smoke exposure chronic obstructive pulmonary disease male patients: evidence from cross-sectional, multi-omic and clinical studies.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a chronic pulmonary disease, with aging and secondhand smoke exposure serving as 2 major risk factors. Serum C-reactive protein (SCRP), a canonical marker of systemic inflammation, has been implicated in COPD progression, but its specific molecular signatures and pathogenic pathways in the context of aging and SHS have not been systematically delineated.
papers.summary: This study investigates the molecular patterns associated with serum C-reactive protein (SCRP) in male COPD patients, focusing on the combined effects of aging and secondhand smoke exposure. Using cross-sectional, multi-omic, and clinical data, the authors identify distinct molecular signatures and pathways linked to SCRP, providing insights into the systemic inflammatory mechanisms in this specific COPD subgroup.

papers.title: Identification and clinical evaluation of diagnostic biomarkers for ischemic cardiomyopathy based on machine learning and transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Ischemic cardiomyopathy (ICM) is a leading cause of heart failure, yet precise molecular tools for potential diagnosis remain limited. This study aims to identify and clinically evaluate novel diagnostic biomarkers for ICM by integrating comprehensive transcriptomic analysis, machine learning algorithms, and real-world serological assessment.
papers.summary: This study identifies novel diagnostic biomarkers for ischemic cardiomyopathy by combining transcriptomic analysis with machine learning, and validates them through serological assessment in clinical samples. The findings offer potential molecular tools for improving ICM diagnosis.

papers.title: A multi-level machine learning pipeline for prediction and prioritization of hybrid insulin peptides in type 1 diabetes.
papers.abstract: Hybrid insulin peptides (HIPs) are neoepitopes involved in type 1 diabetes (T1D), but their complete repertoire remains unknown. The vast combinatorial space makes experimental screening unfeasible and requires bioinformatics-based prioritization. We developed a multi-level machine learning pipeline for ranking HIP candidates. First, 36 physicochemical and junction-specific features were computed for a reference library of 240 HIPs with known enzyme-linked immunospot (ELISPOT) reactivity, and a baseline Ridge regression model was trained. Next, all possible HIP candidates with 7-9 amino acid r
papers.summary: The authors developed a multi-level machine learning pipeline to predict and prioritize hybrid insulin peptides (HIPs), which are neoepitopes implicated in type 1 diabetes. By training a Ridge regression model on physicochemical and junction-specific features from a reference library of 240 HIPs with known ELISPOT reactivity, they aim to rank the vast combinatorial space of HIP candidates for experimental screening. This bioinformatics approach addresses the infeasibility of exhaustive experimental testing and could accelerate T1D epitope discovery.

papers.title: Integrated multi-omics analysis reveals dendritic cell centered regulatory networks and therapeutic targets in necrotizing enterocolitis.
papers.abstract: Necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) is a severe inflammatory intestinal disease predominantly affecting premature infants and is characterized by immune dysregulation and epithelial barrier disruption. However, the cellular communication networks and key molecular regulators underlying NEC pathogenesis remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study uses an integrated multi-omics approach to uncover dendritic cell-centered regulatory networks in necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC), identifying key molecular regulators and potential therapeutic targets. The findings highlight the central role of dendritic cells in NEC pathogenesis and offer new avenues for treatment.

papers.title: Quaternion-based recurrent neural networks and machine learning for 3D modeling of superficial femoral artery dynamics: a theoretical framework for enhanced treatment outcomes.
papers.abstract: The superficial femoral artery (SFA) is highly susceptible to atherosclerotic disease, with restenosis rates which are exceeding 30%-50% following endovascular intervention. Current diagnostic approaches including two-dimensional angiography and duplex ultrasound are failing to capture the complex three-dimensional (3D) spatiotemporal dynamics of vessel remodeling during physiological motion. This theoretical framework is integrating quaternion-based recurrent neural networks (QRNNs) with machine learning pipelines to model dynamic 3D changes in SFA geometry from serial imaging data or continu
papers.summary: This paper proposes a theoretical framework combining quaternion-based recurrent neural networks with machine learning to model the 3D spatiotemporal dynamics of the superficial femoral artery, aiming to improve prediction of vessel remodeling and treatment outcomes. The approach addresses limitations of current 2D imaging by capturing complex 3D changes during physiological motion, potentially reducing high restenosis rates after endovascular intervention.

papers.title: Policy aware fusion of educational and economic indicators for public health curriculum optimization.
papers.abstract: The optimization of public health curricula requires the effective integration of heterogeneous educational, socio economic, behavioral, and course context indicators under policy related constraints. Traditional curriculum design approaches often rely on static rules or isolated educational measurements, making it difficult to capture dynamic learner course interactions, policy consistency, and uncertainty in real world online learning environments. To address these challenges, this study proposes a policy aware framework, termed the Policy Driven Indicator Integrator, for supporting public h
papers.summary: This paper proposes a policy-aware framework, the Policy Driven Indicator Integrator, to optimize public health curricula by integrating educational, socioeconomic, behavioral, and course context data under policy constraints. The framework aims to overcome limitations of static curriculum design by capturing dynamic learner interactions and uncertainty in online learning environments.

papers.title: SiaRNA: a siamese neural network with bidirectional cross-attention for pairwise siRNA-mRNA efficacy prediction.
papers.abstract: Small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics have extraordinary potential for targeted gene silencing. They mediate post-transcriptional gene regulation by binding to complementary messenger RNA (mRNA) sequences and degrading them, thereby preventing the production of unwanted proteins. Recent machine learning and deep learning frameworks for predicting siRNA efficacy have only achieved moderate success as these models solely rely either on handcrafted features or on sequential relations and therefore cannot capture the full complexity of siRNA-mRNA interactions.
papers.summary: The paper introduces SiaRNA, a siamese neural network with bidirectional cross-attention that predicts siRNA-mRNA efficacy by jointly modeling their interaction. It addresses limitations of prior models that relied only on handcrafted features or sequential relations, potentially improving therapeutic target selection.

papers.title: Triglyceride-glucose index and hyperhomocysteinemia within a cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic biomarker network: insights from interpretable machine learning and epidemiological modeling.
papers.abstract: Although the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is an established surrogate marker of insulin resistance and metabolic burden, its relationship with hyperhomocysteinemia (HHcy) within the cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework remains insufficiently understood. This study aimed to investigate the association between TyG and HHcy and to prioritize CKM-related biomarkers using interpretable machine learning and epidemiological modeling.
papers.summary: This study investigates the link between the triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and hyperhomocysteinemia (HHcy) within a cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) framework, using interpretable machine learning and epidemiological modeling. It finds an association between TyG and HHcy and prioritizes CKM-related biomarkers, offering insights into metabolic and cardiovascular risk assessment.

papers.title: Admission laboratory parameters for early risk stratification after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage: a machine learning analysis of real-world data.
papers.abstract: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Early risk stratification is essential for treatment planning and prognostication, yet neurological assessment may be limited in sedated or critically ill patients. Routine admission laboratory parameters may provide additional prognostic information and improve machine learning (ML)-based outcome prediction.
papers.summary: This study uses machine learning on real-world data to evaluate whether routine admission laboratory parameters can improve early risk stratification after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). The findings suggest that these readily available lab values add prognostic value, potentially aiding outcome prediction in sedated or critically ill patients where neurological assessment is limited.

papers.title: SHAP-interpretable machine learning integrating exposures and multi-omics reveals immune alterations and biomarkers in COPD-lung cancer comorbidity.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and lung cancer (LC) frequently co-occur and share environmental and biological determinants, yet their cross-scale associations remain incompletely understood. Artificial intelligence and machine learning-based integration of exposome and multi-omics data provide new opportunities for dissecting this complex comorbidity.
papers.summary: This study uses SHAP-interpretable machine learning to integrate environmental exposures and multi-omics data, revealing immune alterations and potential biomarkers associated with COPD-lung cancer comorbidity. The approach identifies key cross-scale associations that may improve understanding of shared mechanisms and aid in diagnosis or risk assessment.

papers.title: A biologically structured hierarchical vision transformer-CNN framework for robust tomato leaf disease classification.
papers.abstract: Precise and reliable diagnosis of leaf diseases in tomato is essential for enhancing crop cultivation and minimizing agricultural losses. While deep learning models have performed well on benchmark datasets, the majority of present techniques rely on flat multi-class classification, which predicts all disease categories simultaneously. Such formulations promotes inter-class confusion, particularly when biologically different diseases with similar visual symptoms are learned within a same model. To overcome this constraint, we propose a biologically structured hierarchical deep learning framewo
papers.summary: This paper proposes a biologically structured hierarchical deep learning framework that combines vision transformers and CNNs for tomato leaf disease classification. By organizing disease categories hierarchically based on biological relationships, the approach reduces inter-class confusion among visually similar diseases, improving classification robustness.

papers.title: Generative AI-augmented transcriptomic and microbiome analysis across inflammatory and fibrotic disease states in Crohn's disease.
papers.abstract: Intestinal fibrosis is a major complication of Crohn's disease (CD), a subtype of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) driven by chronic inflammation and resulting in irreversible structural damage requiring surgery. However, the molecular differences between inflammatory and fibrotic CD remain poorly defined.
papers.summary: This study uses generative AI to analyze transcriptomic and microbiome data from Crohn's disease patients, aiming to distinguish between inflammatory and fibrotic disease states. The approach identifies molecular signatures that differentiate these conditions, potentially improving diagnosis and treatment targeting fibrosis.

papers.title: TPT: a compact CNN-transformer encoder for efficient microbial small protein modeling.
papers.abstract: Microbial small proteins, encoded by small open reading frames (smORFs), play essential roles in antimicrobial activity, metabolic regulation, and signaling pathways. However, their short length and rapid evolutionary rate present significant challenges for computational modeling.
papers.summary: This paper introduces TPT, a compact CNN-transformer hybrid encoder designed to improve computational modeling of microbial small proteins, which are difficult to analyze due to their short length and rapid evolution. The model aims to efficiently capture features from these proteins, potentially aiding in functional prediction and downstream analyses.

papers.title: Representations of facial features and surface quality in monkey area TE compared to neural network models.
papers.abstract: The shape and spacing of facial features are essential for the perception of emotional expressions and the identification of individuals. The surface quality of faces, such as skin texture, eye twinkle, and hair gloss, is valuable for estimating health status. A previous fMRI study in monkeys revealed that regions selective for faces overlapped regions selective for object gloss in the central inferior temporal (IT) cortex, suggesting that the surface quality of faces is processed in area TE. However, the representation of facial surface quality has not been directly examined in this area. To
papers.summary: This study investigates how monkey area TE represents facial features and surface quality, comparing these representations to neural network models. The findings suggest that area TE encodes both facial shape and surface properties, with neural network models providing a useful framework for understanding these representations.

papers.title: A generative AI multi-agent framework with integrated XAI governance for cancer diagnostics: from multi-omics interpretation to lifestyle risk stratification.
papers.abstract: Cancer diagnostics is being reshaped by rapid advances in artificial intelligence, yet a persistent gap separates computational performance from clinical trust. Systematic reviews confirm that 83% of XAI studies in oncology excluded clinicians from development or evaluation, 87% lacked rigorous assessment of XAI explanations, and no universally accepted quality metrics for XAI outputs currently exist. Concurrently, generative AI (GenAI) is entering oncology at an unprecedented pace, yet it operates largely without formal interpretability governance.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a generative AI multi-agent framework for cancer diagnostics that integrates explainable AI (XAI) governance to bridge the gap between computational performance and clinical trust. The framework combines multi-omics interpretation with lifestyle risk stratification, addressing the lack of clinician involvement and standardized XAI quality metrics in current oncology AI systems.

papers.title: DFN-kcr: a dual-branch deep learning model with attention-guided fusion for predicting lysine crotonylation sites in human non-histone proteins.
papers.abstract: Lysine crotonylation (Kcr) is extensively present in human non-histone proteins and plays a critical regulatory role in essential biological processes, including cell signaling and metabolic regulation. However, conventional wet-lab approaches for Kcr site identification are costly, time-consuming, and ill-suited for large-scale profiling. Although computational prediction methods have garnered increasing attention in recent years, there remains a notable lack of efficient and specialized tools tailored specifically for Kcr site prediction in human non-histone proteins.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This paper introduces DFN-kcr, a dual-branch deep learning model with attention-guided fusion for predicting lysine crotonylation (Kcr) sites in human non-histone proteins. The model addresses the lack of specialized computational tools for this task, offering a more efficient alternative to costly and time-consuming wet-lab experiments.
